as_told.title: Immaculate Constellation actually an old NSC-owned mission

plain: A secret program called Immaculate Constellation, said to gather military images of unexplained objects, is run by the Defense Department but kept at the White House. That is what the journalist Michael Shellenberger tells Michels, and he said the same to a House Oversight Committee hearing, Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Exposing the Truth, on 13 November 2024. If he is right, a program on UFOs would sit at the very top of government. The program's name comes from an unsigned report that Shellenberger gave to Congress. Rep. Nancy Mace entered it into the hearing record as a document from the Pentagon. The report calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department. A former Defense Department official named Matthew Brown later said he wrote it, and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report calls the program "an Unacknowledged Special Access Program (USAP)", meaning a classified program whose very existence is not admitted. It says the program collects images "utilizing tasked and untasked U.S. military-intelligence resources", but it does not say which office runs it or holds it. The White House part is something Shellenberger says he was told after he published, and at the hearing he added, "that is a single source, and I do not have multiple sources to verify that." Brown tells Michels a different version: the program is "ran out of and owned by the National Security Council out of the White House", and it is an old mission that began before 2017.

discussion.by: Immaculate Constellation report (anonymous, entered into the House Oversight hearing record, 13 November 2024)
discussion.text: An unsigned report that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress and Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, later said he wrote it; and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report calls the program "an Unacknowledged Special Access Program (USAP)" collecting imagery "utilizing tasked and untasked U.S. military-intelligence resources", and does not say which office manages or holds it. The White House comes from what Michael Shellenberger says he was told after he published, from one source by his own account at the hearing, and the National Security Council from Matthew Brown, who later said he wrote the report.
